sources.entry: macOSLucidaGrande - A small utility to set Lucida Grande as your Mac's system UI font.

summary.one_liner: A small macOS utility that switches the Mac's system UI font between Lucida Grande and San Francisco (or Helvetica Neue on Yosemite).
summary.what_it_does: The utility switches the Mac's system font to Lucida Grande and back, according to the README. On macOS Mojave, High Sierra, Sierra and OS X El Capitan it toggles between Lucida Grande and San Francisco. On OS X Yosemite it toggles between Lucida Grande and Helvetica Neue. The README says switching works without modifying system files. The README lists two known issues: truncated text may overlap in Safari and Firefox on the older supported releases, and password fields appear blank while typing. It also credits Alexander Schreiber's earlier LucidaGrandeYosemite and LucidaGrandeElCapitan projects as the basis for its font patches. The README does not describe install steps beyond a download link.
use_cases: Change the macOS system font to Lucida Grande
Switch back to San Francisco system font
Restore the classic Lucida Grande look on an older Mac
Compare system UI fonts on macOS without editing system files
notable: Toggles between Lucida Grande and San Francisco (or Helvetica Neue on Yosemite)
Says it does not modify system files
Builds on Alexander Schreiber's LucidaGrandeYosemite and LucidaGrandeElCapitan font patches
caveats: Known issue: truncated text may overlap in Safari and Firefox on Mojave, High Sierra, Sierra and El Capitan
Known issue: password fields look blank while typing (Issue #2)
Targets older macOS releases from OS X El Capitan through macOS Mojave; the README does not mention newer versions
